newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's insurance market lures Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Israel's insurance market lures Palestinians.

text.p: Palestinian investors hoping to tap into Israel's lucrative insurance market are seeking a joint venture with Israeli-Arab businessmen, the project's legal adviser said on Wednesday.

Mazen Qubty, who is also an investor in the project, said six West Bank and Gaza-based insurance companies agreed to set up al-Fanar insurance company as a private share-holding firm capitalised at $10 million.
"Al-Fanar will be an Israeli company with Palestinian capital," Qubty told Reuters. "This is the first time that Palestinians will invest (in insurance) in Israel."

Qubty said the company, which will have headquarters in Arab East Jerusalem and in Nazareth, the largest Arab town in Israel, has received initial approval from Israeli authorities and was expected to begin work early next year.

He said the six Palestinian insurance firms would provide $4.6 million of the company's capital. The Arab Bank and the Arab Palestinian investment company (APIC) have agreed to pay $500,000 each and the rest will be covered by Israeli-Arab businessmen.
Founders were in contact with Arab businessmen from Israel to arrange the investment, and a meeting will be held on May 9 to discuss the subject.
"We have started contacts with Palestinians in Israel who have expressed readiness to participate in the joint investment," Qubty said, referring to Arabs with Israeli citizenship.
"We expect the subscriptions to go over the $10 million capital," he said.

Qubty said the company would primarily target the Israeli Arab sector's insurance market, which makes up between seven to eight percent of Israel's $10.3 billion insurance market, not including life insurance.
The combined West Bank and Gaza insurance market is estimated at about $50 million, he said.
"We expect that within three years we will have two thirds of (the Israeli-Arab) sector, which is about $500 million," Qubty said.

Israel's 900,000 Arab citizens presently buy their insurance mainly from Jewish-owned companies. East Jerusalem's 160,000 Arabs also rely on Israeli insurance companies or on agents of West Bank companies.
Qubty said founders believe the new venture's marketing strategy, reinsurance terms and other advantages will give it a competitive edge over Israeli companies already operating in the Arab sector.

The company will also target Palestinians in Arab East Jerusalem, who under Israeli laws may not buy insurance from companies based in areas under Palestinian self-rule and find Israeli insurance companies too expensive.
Qubty said the company hopes to reinvest its profits in the Arab sector.
"The company is expected to be a success and hopefully it will help induce new initiatives for other joint ventures in the future," Qubty said.
